notes.heading: Fiscal calendar
notes.text: FY2023 ended September 3, 2023 and had 53 weeks. FY2024 ended September 1, 2024 and FY2025 ended August 31, 2025, both with 52 weeks. FY2024 revenue growth compares the reported 52-week year with the preceding 53-week year. FY2023 growth requires an earlier comparison year.

notes.heading: Retail margins
notes.text: Operating and net margins use total revenue. Merchandise gross margin uses net sales and excludes membership fees, following Costco’s definition.

notes.heading: Debt and leases
notes.text: Costco describes short-term bank borrowings as immaterial without publishing a balance. That leaves total current borrowings, net debt, current share of borrowings and net debt to EBITDA unresolved. Current maturities of long-term debt are reported separately. Three FY2023 lease components appear in the PDF but have no matched SEC Company Facts entry in the selected filings. The published aggregate lease balance is shown from the PDF.

source_note: Amounts are checked against Costco’s FY2024 and FY2025 Form 10-K tags and corresponding issuer-hosted annual reports. Net sales, membership fees and aggregate lease liabilities use the printed statements as their quantified source.

location_growth.assumption_note: The 4% existing-site sales growth, 50%/80%/100% sales ramp, $100 million per net opening and 3% capex inflation are illustrative. Sales per mature warehouse is a proxy calibrated from reported consolidated net sales, which includes ancillary and e-commerce sales. Membership fees follow the Base schedule. The $3.098 billion of other cash capex is the FY2025 residual after 24 net openings at the assumed cost. It covers the existing estate, relocations and other projects in aggregate. The forecast uses this cash capex basis. FY2025 comparable sales grew about 6%. The FY2025 filing indicated up to 30 net FY2026 openings (35 gross less five relocations) and a $6.0–$6.5 billion cash capex plan.

valuation.assumption_note:
Historical valuation at the October 9, 2025 close using the FY2025 run rate and the September 30 share count. The forecast starts at the quote date. Merchandise sales and membership fees grow separately, then add to total revenue. The Base case assumes fee revenue grows 7% in Year 1 and tapers to 5.5%. Paid members grew from 76.2 to 81.0 million in FY2025. Costco attributes roughly 40% of FY2025 fee revenue growth to the September 2024 fee increase. Sales growth assumptions reflect a mix of warehouse expansion and comparable sales.

About 91% of starting operating costs are modeled as variable, based on the share of merchandise costs in FY2025 operating costs. Volume represents merchandise activity for the cost forecast. The starting variable cost growth rates are calibrated to Year 5 margins of 3.4%, 4.1% and 4.65% in Bear, Base and Bull. Editing a driver changes those margins. Tax and D&A are anchored to FY2025. The Base case implies approximately $6.45 billion of Year 1 capital investment, near the upper end of the $6.0–$6.5 billion FY2026 cash capex plan. Forecast investment allows for finance-leased assets. The working capital assumptions reflect low net merchandise inventory and the variability of supplier financing.

The 7.25–9.25% discount rates are scenario assumptions, with an 8.25% Base case and a 4.14% 10-year Treasury benchmark on the quote date. Terminal growth of 2.5–3.5% and terminal returns on invested capital of 16–25% are long-run assumptions. The bridge treats cash at carrying value and adds short-term debt securities and deposits at carrying value because their interest income sits outside operating profit. Operating lease expense stays in operating costs. Finance lease liabilities are included in modeled debt.
